title: Priority under a rate-limited link
summary: The rover-Gateway leg is limited to 4000 bytes/s in the contact plan (so ION meters bundles onto the link at that rate) and to 4400 bytes/s with a 65536-byte drop-tail queue in the emulator (10 % above the contact rate for LTP and UDP header overhead). At 2 s the rover queues 40 BULK envelopes of 3000 bytes (about 30 s of link time); from 6 s it sends five small envelopes each of CRITICAL, HIGH, NORMAL and LOW, 3 s apart. ION's bpclm serves the urgent queue (expedited class: CRITICAL, HIGH) before any other, and shares the remaining capacity between the standard queue (NORMAL) and the bulk queue (LOW, BULK) in proportion 2:1 by bytes sent (bpv7/daemon/bpclm.c; docs/MAPPING-PROFILE.md). CRITICAL, HIGH and NORMAL are expected to arrive ahead of the BULK backlog; LOW shares ION's bulk queue with BULK and is expected to wait behind it.

criteria.text: Every rover envelope handed to ION is received at Earth
Every Earth command handed to ION is received at the rover
Every received envelope is byte-identical to the envelope handed to ION
CRITICAL and HIGH envelopes (PING replies included) arrive within 4.0 s despite the BULK backlog
NORMAL envelopes arrive within 4.0 s despite the BULK backlog
Every CRITICAL, HIGH and NORMAL envelope arrives before at least one BULK envelope that was sent before it
The slowest CRITICAL or HIGH envelope is faster than the median BULK envelope
LOW envelopes (ION bulk class, same as BULK) do not overtake BULK envelopes sent before them
The emulator queue never overflowed (the backlog was held in ION)
Every send uses the class of service of SPEC-DIGEST 7.5 for its priority
No duplicate or unknown envelope is received
Largest wait in the emulator queue, rover-gateway (informative)

conformance.how: partial: higher-priority envelopes forwarded ahead of a lower-priority backlog under constrained throughput (S4-5 to S4-8); no authorized degradation policy (PBS-QOS-MAP-01) is defined or applied

partial: one ION class of service per priority per SPEC-DIGEST 7.5 and docs/MAPPING-PROFILE.md (S4-11); LOW and BULK share the bulk class (S4-9). One static mapping, with no network state input and no policy version
priority handling observed end to end
priority byte unchanged (S4-3) and mapped to ION class of service; the mapping profile with the four PBS-DTN-MAP-02 Section 5 items is docs/MAPPING-PROFILE.md
4000 bytes/s contact rate, 4400 bytes/s emulated link
